messages:
Maya: Heads up — customer on hosted-api reporting widespread 5xx after this morning's canary roll. Multiple apps seeing 503s and some auth failures. Request id: req_8a3f9b2d

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: release=canary-2026-03-12-42 by Ben at 2790012000

Maya: Pasted a customer error sample:
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"upstream timeout","trace":"req_8a3f9b2d","stage":"kv-loader"}
```

Ben: On it. Can someone drop the grafana link for the 5xx spike?

observability-bot: Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosted-api/5xx-dashboard?from=now-1h&to=now (prod, canary filter applied)

Emily: Looking at traces — canary nodes show a sharp latency tail and increased inflight. 5xx rate up ~35% vs baseline in ap-northeast-1.

Alice: I think the canary toggled the KV cache prefill path: `model.orch.kvcache_prefill=true` was enabled for the canary group. That codepath hits auth/loader earlier and may block under backpressure. I missed that hit to the auth proxy when gating the flag.

Carlos: Repro steps from my laptop (same region):
```
$ curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
> HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
> x-upstream-error: kv-cache-miss
{"error":"upstream timeout","stage":"kv-loader","trace":"req_9b2c..."}
```
Headers show lots of queued requests on canary nodes.

Ben: Can someone confirm ingress and auth-proxy queueing? Might be a shedder mismatch or missing rate cap for this new path.

Emily: Confirmed: canary instances report kernel prefetch CPU saturation + ingress max-inflight at default 500. With the new prefill path each request opens extra blocking ops; canary backend saturating. Two options: scale canary horizontally OR rollback the canary flag. Scaling would take longer; rollback is faster.

Maya: Customer wants ETA ASAP — they're seeing failed requests for ~12 minutes and some billing implications.

Alice: Agree rollback recommended. I'll prepare to flip the flag back.

Ben: Initiating rollback now: `redwoodctl deploy rollback --target=canary-2026-03-12-42 --confirm` (running)

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: release_id=canary-2026-03-12-42, initiated_by=Ben, action_id=rbk-2790012345

Carlos: I'm watching ingress logs — after rollback start tail, 5xxs already trending down on canary IPs.

observability-bot: 5xx rate (prod + canary) decreased from 8.2% -> 1.0% over last 90s. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosted-api/5xx-dashboard?from=now-5m&to=now

Ben: Patch to rollout config: ensure `model.orch.kvcache_prefill` gated behind `preflight.authpath_check` and default false for canary. I'll push change after rollback completes.

Alice: PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/redwood/orch/pull/3487 — adds gate + unit test and a canary traffic cap of 10% so we don't overwhelm auth path next time.

support-bot: Customer ticket #4567 updated: note="rollback in progress, 5xx spike correlated with canary kvcache_prefill flag, investigating", status=investigating

Maya: I updated the customer: rollback in progress, expected restoration within 2-3 minutes, apologies for the disruption. :pray:

Ben: Post-rollback checks look good; 5xxs back to baseline, latency tail cleared on canary and prod.

Emily: Follow-ups: add shedder metrics for kv-cache ops, add canary preflight for flags touching auth/loader, enforce canary traffic cap by default.

Ben: I'll own the postmortem and runbook updates.

Maya: Thanks team. Please drop a short summary in the incident channel when postmortem ready. :thumbsup:
